title: Muscat / Zanzibar
hook: 1800 → 1880. Two fixed dots; compare the reconstruction's labels.

knows: two points can be located on a map
doesNotKnow: how this reconstruction classifies Muscat / Zanzibar in 1800 and 1880, and what that comparison cannot establish

misconception: A historical map's region labels directly establish exact borders, continuous control and the history of everyone inside.
objective: Compare the source's labels at two fixed points in 1800 and 1880; distinguish the observed map pattern from claims about its cause or legitimacy.

claims.text: Muscat area anchor: 58.41, 23.43 (17.8 km from the nominal location); Zanzibar area anchor: 38.902642, -6.282459 (35.6 km from the nominal location). Modern place names orient the fixed comparison points, not historical settlement names or exact city centres.
claims.source: tools/history-maps/cases.mjs: nominal WGS84 longitude/latitude points; generate.mjs areaAnchor prefers the nearest point covered by both snapshots within 75 km, without selecting for an answer. map.json records nominal and actual coordinates and the offset. A place name is not an ancient-settlement claim.

claims.text: The 1800 and 1880 stages are clipped Mercator paths from these GeoJSON snapshots, with all matched NAME labels retained: [[["Oman"],["Zanzibar"]],[["Oman"],["Sultanate of Zanzibar"]]]. Map key and SVG titles use these labels; NAME is not SUBJECTO.
claims.source: Ring directions normalised for d3 spherical exteriors/holes; coordinates and feature order retained. https://github.com/aourednik/historical-basemaps/blob/da7a4b735ecef70aebdc9c73e409d8a2500d50f3/geojson/world_1800.geojson (SHA-256 51fcb6b1f1c361956a3fc24a9c646844ff88754842aa113780428fb4abcd5f2c); GeoJSON features [[41],[114]]; https://github.com/aourednik/historical-basemaps/blob/da7a4b735ecef70aebdc9c73e409d8a2500d50f3/geojson/world_1880.geojson (SHA-256 4751e30d881d60d31479f5d016ff4d9c1df47e9bb18efaa3a5086601f68f76dc); GeoJSON features [[81],[60]]

claims.text: At the two points, 1800 has different labels and 1880 has different labels. This supports the prediction answer and first reveal sentence.
claims.source: tools/history-maps/generate.mjs: geoContains on every feature; sorted unique NAME sets, exact set equality; missing sets stay unlabelled. https://github.com/aourednik/historical-basemaps/blob/da7a4b735ecef70aebdc9c73e409d8a2500d50f3/geojson/world_1800.geojson (SHA-256 51fcb6b1f1c361956a3fc24a9c646844ff88754842aa113780428fb4abcd5f2c); GeoJSON features [[41],[114]]; https://github.com/aourednik/historical-basemaps/blob/da7a4b735ecef70aebdc9c73e409d8a2500d50f3/geojson/world_1880.geojson (SHA-256 4751e30d881d60d31479f5d016ff4d9c1df47e9bb18efaa3a5086601f68f76dc); GeoJSON features [[81],[60]]

claims.text: The maps are approximate reconstructions. Two snapshots do not date a transition, establish continuity, explain causes, or settle present-day claims; an unlabelled dot does not prove empty land.
claims.source: https://github.com/aourednik/historical-basemaps/blob/da7a4b735ecef70aebdc9c73e409d8a2500d50f3/README.md, sections Conceptual limitations and disputed territories / Polygons; two-endpoint inference limit. Stage caption, reveal, hook 'reconstruction', and prediction wording are covered here. Cultural and research reviews remain required.

claims.text: A region looks larger on this Mercator crop. Is that enough to compare its land area? Answer: No; use an equal-area method or spherical calculation Mercator distorts area. This map exercise compares labels at points, not the sizes of territories.
claims.source: https://github.com/aourednik/historical-basemaps/blob/da7a4b735ecef70aebdc9c73e409d8a2500d50f3/README.md (source limitations); tools/history-maps/generate.mjs recalls[7]. Interpret the dataset fields and projection, not historical causes.

recall.question: A region looks larger on this Mercator crop. Is that enough to compare its land area?
options: No; use an equal-area method or spherical calculation
Yes, if both colours are bright
recall.why: Mercator distorts area. This map exercise compares labels at points, not the sizes of territories.

careLine: Source NAME labels are classifications, not statements of legitimate sovereignty, ethnicity, religion, language or absence of people. Modern place names are orientation aids only. Retain missing coverage and overlapping labels.
